title: Add a '--lockfile' flag to 'rig proj sync'
description:
This commit adds a `--lockfile` argument for precise control over what `rig proj sync` installs from. Together with `--library` it can be used to install a lock file into a library from any directory, e.g. in a build job that only needs the installed packages.

I expect this to be a pretty niche feature, so I haven't added much in the way of documentation.

Unit and integration tests are included.

title: Authentication
description:
## Authenticated repositories

rig now sends HTTP basic auth to private CRAN-like repositories and Posit Package Manager instances, for all of its downloads (`rig pkg`, `rig proj`, `rig ppm`, ...). It works like pak's authenticated repositories, with the same netrc file, keyring keys and PPM token file, so credentials set up for pak also work in rig.

Credentials are looked up per URL, first match wins:

1. a password in the URL (`--with-repos` only, kept in memory)
2. `RIG_REPO_<NAME>_USERNAME` / `RIG_REPO_<NAME>_PASSWORD`
3. a PPM SSO token from `~/.ppm/tokens.toml`
4. a netrc file
5. the system credential store (only for URLs with a username)

rig never stores passwords: `rig repos add` and `rproj.toml` reject URLs with one, and `--with-repos` URLs have it removed. Requests are sent without userinfo in the URL, so passwords don't show up in error messages. 401/403
errors suggest `rig auth status`.

New commands: `rig auth login` (PPM SSO in the browser, or `--username` to save a password in the keyring), `rig auth logout`, `rig auth status` and `rig auth token`. They take a URL or a repository name. Without one, they use `PACKAGEMANAGER_ADDRESS`.

Closes #394.

title: rig add: create the site library on demand
description:
## Summary

New `rig add --with-site-library` option: it creates the site library (`R_HOME/site-library`) of the newly installed R version. R only uses the site library if this directory exists, and then puts it on `.libPaths()` after the user library.

- New `rig add` flags: `--with-site-library` creates the directory; `--without-site-library` (the default) does not. The two flags conflict.
- New `create_site_library()` helper in `src/library.rs`, called from `sc_add` on macOS, Linux and Windows. On macOS it runs before the admin-mode permission fix, so that fix also covers the new directory. The path logic is in `rhome_from_system_profile()` and `create_site_library_in()`, which have unit tests.
- pak installation is unchanged; pak still goes into the user library.
- Updated `src/help/add.md` (regenerated `src/help-generated.in`) and `NEWS.md`.
- BATS tests check that `rig add --with-site-library` creates the directory, and that a plain `rig add` does not.

## Testing

- `cargo build`, `cargo clippy`, `cargo fmt` and `cargo xtask gen-help --check` are clean, and `cargo test` passes on macOS and Linux.
- Linux (Docker, admin mode): `rig add 4.5.1` created no site library; `rig add 4.4.3 --with-site-library` created `/opt/R/4.4.3/lib/R/site-library`.
- Tested `rig add` by hand on macOS (before the default changed).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Emit only one error for a package whose downloads all fail
description:
Previously a package with more than one URL in the lockfile printed an error for every URL that answered with a bad status (e.g. 404 because it has moved to the Archive), then another for "all download URLs failed", and one more for the package, even when a later URL worked.

As of this commit we emit only a single error (listing each URL and status) if they *all* fail, and log other failures at info or debug level.

In practice this condition was hard to hit because `rig` doesn't create multiple URL entries under most conditions, but I ran into it when constructing lockfiles manually.

Unit tests are included.

title: Normalise modes in unpacked archives to more closely match R
description:
Previously we left package archives's mode intact, which meant that e.g. PPM binaries had 775 for a shared library and 664 for the `DESCRIPTION` file. This is generally fine for single-user caches, but it's not the right security model for a cache you want to share more broadly (e.g. on a multiuser machine).

This commit moves us closer to the behaviour of `R CMD INSTALL`, and thus to tools like `pak`, `renv`, and `packrat`.

~~Note that tar and zip archives are handled slightly differently since zip has to be walked after the fact.~~

Unit tests are included and make up the majority of the diff.

title: Add --cache-dir to override the location of rig's cache
description:
This commit adds a new `--cache-dir` flag, along with the corresponding `RIG_CACHE_DIR` environment variable and `cache-dir` config entry, with the usual precedence. This lets users keep rig's cache in a directory of their choice instead of the platform default, without having to override `XDG_CACHE_HOME` for the whole process.

Because the directory can be anywhere, `rig cache clean` is now more careful, and only cleans directories that look like it created them. To accomplish this, we use a convention borrowed from `uv` and write a `CACHEDIR.TAG` file into custom `--cache-dir` directories when creating them.

Unit and integration tests are included, as is documentation. There are also some clarifications to the documentation around the effect of `--no-cache` on log files.

title: Add a '--library' flag to 'rig proj sync'
description:
Previously we documented a `--library` flag for this subcommand, but it didn't actually exist.

This commit implements it, specifically targeting testing and integrating `rig` into other tools that might not want its other environment files.

Unit and integration tests are included.

title: Do not activate project for R version mismatch
description: Closes #450.

title: Build from source when a binary URL serves a source package fallback
description:
Posit Package Manager will serve source packages at binary URLs if there is no built binary available. This commit ensures we detect this and don't accidentally unpack an unbuilt source package into the cache.

The metadata feed generally prevents hitting this in pratice, but it's good hardening to do if we want to support PPM instances other than P3M in the future.

Unit tests are included.

title: Add a tutorial for migrating renv projects to rig
description:
## Summary

Adds a tutorial for users considering a move from renv to `rig proj`, with links from the Tutorials navigation and the R projects guide.

The article serves two audiences: readers comparing the tools and readers ready to migrate a working project. It explains the separation between requirements in `rproj.toml` and the resolved environment in `rproj.lock`, then walks through backing up the project, deactivating renv, importing and reviewing dependencies, locking and syncing, and checking the result in Positron or RStudio.

The tutorial also calls out the experimental status of `rig proj` and the limits of the existing import: exact versions become compatible-version requirements, package-source information is not retained, and renv's startup activation is not removed.

## Follow-up

Writing this tutorial motivated a proposal for `rig proj renv migrate` and improvements to renv import, tracked separately in #471. This PR is documentation-only.

title: Import repositories from renv.lock
description:
`rig proj renv import` now reads the package repositories of an renv.lock and turns them into `[[repository]]` entries, instead of leaving every package to resolve from the built-in CRAN. We also make an effort to map known CRAN and Bioconductor aliases to the built-in ones, and turn off these built-in repositories if the `renv.lock` in question doesn't use them (which matches how renv behaves).

In addition, we now warn when packages from other sources (e.g. GitHub, GitLab, local) will need manual adjustment.

This is progress towards some of the issues raised in #471.

Unit tests are included.

title: Import git-based package sources from renv.lock
description:
This commit allows `rig proj renv import` to import renv.lock files with packages from GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket and git.

This is progress towards some of the issues raised in #471.

Unit tests are included.

title: Add rig add --without-default and Rscript-<version> quick links
description:
## Summary

- **`Rscript-<version>` quick links**: rig now creates `Rscript-<version>` links (`Rscript-<version>.exe` shims on Windows) next to the `R-<version>` ones, whenever the quick links are updated. They are cleaned up in the same places as the `R-<version>` links: the dangling-link cleanup after `rig rm`, and `rig system user-mode` / `clean-admin-r`.
- **`rig add --without-default`**: does not make the new R version the default, even if there is no default yet, so the plain `R` and `Rscript` links are not created; only the versioned links are. On macOS in admin mode the CRAN installer creates `/usr/local/bin/R` and `Rscript` itself, so rig removes them after the install, unless they existed before. `rig default` can still set a default later.
- Docs: help for `rig add`, `rig default` and `rig system make-links` (regenerated `src/help-generated.in`), `NEWS.md`, and a `Rscript-<version>` example in the tutorial pages.
- BATS tests check that `Rscript-<version>` runs the right R version.

On macOS, `Rscript-<version>` is a plain symlink: each CRAN `Rscript` binary has its own versioned `R_HOME` compiled in (e.g. `R.framework/Versions/4.1/Resources`), so it runs its own R version, not the default one.

## Testing

- macOS: `cargo build`, `cargo clippy`, `cargo test` and `cargo xtask gen-help --check` are clean.
- Linux (Docker): `cargo check` is clean, and the link regex unit test passes. End-to-end in admin mode: `rig add 4.5.1 --without-default` created only `R-4.5.1` and `Rscript-4.5.1` and set no default; `Rscript-4.5.1` ran R 4.5.1; `rig default 4.5.1` then created `R`/`Rscript`; `rig rm 4.5.1` removed both versioned links.
- Linux user mode: rig created the right links, but I could not run the portable R in my container, because R itself crashed under Rosetta emulation, independently of the links.
- Windows: not compiled locally; relying on CI.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

description:

* Use `!recordversion` to avoid touching the registry in user mode.

title: Add `rig add --no-default` and `--without-path`
description:
`rig add` makes the first R version it installs the default when no default is set yet (`set_default_if_none`). In user mode that does more than install R: it creates the `R`/`Rscript` quick links, and `rig default` registers the version with RStudio and Positron, which on macOS means installing and loading the `io.r-lib.rig.rstudio-which-r` LaunchAgent that runs `launchctl setenv RSTUDIO_WHICH_R ...` at every login.

RStudio now bundles rig and runs `rig add <version> --user` when a project asks for an R version that is not installed (rstudio/rstudio#19229). From RStudio's side the LaunchAgent is a problem: it outlives RStudio, overrides RStudio's own R selection for every launch from the Dock, and clobbers a user's own `launchctl setenv RSTUDIO_WHICH_R`. The quick links also shadow e.g. Homebrew's R in the user's shell. There is currently no way to ask rig to only install R.

This PR adds `rig add --no-default`, which skips `set_default_if_none` on all three platforms. On Linux the user-mode `R`/`Rscript` aliases are then refreshed only when a default exists (otherwise they would be dangling links into `current/bin`). On Windows `maybe_update_registry_default` already runs only when the `R.exe` shim exists, so nothing else changes there. `rig default <version>` still works afterwards for users who do want the default.

A second commit adds `rig add --without-path`. In user mode rig also puts its quick-link directory on the PATH when it is missing: a line in the shell startup files on macOS and Linux (`check_local_bin_path`), and the directory prepended to the user PATH in the registry on Windows (`add_user_bin_to_path`, from `sc_system_make_links`). That happens on every `rig add`, not only when a default is set, so `--no-default` leaves it in place; `--without-path` skips it. It is a process-wide switch set from the parsed `add` arguments, since the PATH is edited from helpers that take no arguments.

The help text (`src/help/add.md`, regenerated with `make help`) now says what setting the default and the PATH setup involve, and NEWS has an entry.

Verified: `cargo build`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo test --bin rig` (1116 passed, 11 ignored), including a parsing test for both flags. I have not run the bats integration tests.

Once a release includes this, RStudio will pass `--no-default --without-path`; until then it undoes the default-R setup after the install (rstudio/rstudio#19229).

title: treat a missing binary dir as having no aliases on macos
description:
On macOS in user mode, `rig list`, `rig add` and anything else that goes through `sc_get_list_details()` failed with a bare `No such file or directory (os error 2)` when `~/.local/bin` did not exist yet, which is the state of a fresh macOS account that has never installed R with rig. `find_aliases()` in `src/macos.rs` called `read_dir()` on the binary directory unconditionally; the Linux and Windows versions already return an empty list for a missing directory.

This PR splits the directory lookup out of `find_aliases()` into `find_aliases_in(&Path)`, which returns no aliases when the directory is missing, and adds two unit tests for it (missing directory, and a directory with one alias link plus one plain quick link). NEWS has an entry.

Verified: `cargo build`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo test --bin rig` (1117 passed, 11 ignored). With the fixed binary, `HOME=$(mktemp -d) RIG_MODE=user rig list` prints an empty list and `rig add 4.3.999 --user` gets as far as the version lookup, where before both failed immediately.

Fixes #491.

title: Reuse built source packages when checksums are missing
description:
The PACKAGES index of a Posit Package Manager has no checksums for source packages. Previously, this meant that a source package from a private PPM instance ended up with no `RemoteHash` field in the lock and no identifier in the build cache -- and thus rig compiled it again for every library it was installed into.

This is particularly annoying when using using a private PPM instance in place of P3M for an `rproj.toml`, which makes the usual binary machinery metadata unavailable and thus everything gets built from source.

As of this commit, when no checksums are available, rig now computes the sha256 of the downloaded source tarball itself, and identifies it by the version and identity of the package's `LinkingTo` field in the build cache.

(We don't impute a `RemoteHash` and lock time because that would require downloading the file.)

Unit tests are included.

title: feat: Add Amazon Linux 2023 support
description:
Closes #311

Adds AL2023 as a supported distro. The RHEL 9 R builds from Posit are binary-compatible with AL2023, so this maps the platform for version resolution while keeping AL2023 as its own distro for install tooling and repo setup. As discussed in https://github.com/r-lib/rig/issues/311#issuecomment-4174098723,  this uses the P3M "[manylinux](https://posit.co/blog/introducing-portable-linux-r-binary-packages/])" binary repo, rather than distro-specific RHEL 9 PPM binaries, to avoid the EPEL dependency problem.

### Changes

- **`src/common.rs`**: Map `linux-amzn-2023` to `linux-rhel-9` for the r-hub API version resolution
- **`src/linux.rs`**: Add `"amzn"` branch in `select_linux_tools()` with simple `dnf install`, no EPEL
- **`src/data/repos.json`**: Enable `P3M-manylinux` (`manylinux_2_28`) binaries for `"amzn"` on both x86_64 and aarch64

### Testing

Tested on amazonlinux:2023 (aarch64) in Docker:

```
docker run -it --rm --privileged -v $(pwd):/work amazonlinux:2023 bash
dnf install -y /work/r-rig-0.8.00.1.2.rpm
```

After setup:

```
$ rig system detect-platform
Distribution: amzn
Version:      2023

$ rig resolve release
4.5.3 https://cdn.posit.co/r/rhel-9/pkgs/R-4.5.3-1-1.aarch64.rpm

$ rig add release
[INFO] Running "dnf install -y /tmp/rig/R-4.5.3-1-1.aarch64.rpm"
[INFO] Installing pak for R 4.5.3
```

Start R

```
R
```

P3M manylinux repo is configured automatically, and installing R packages correctly pulls in binaries, e.g.:

```r
> getOption('repos')
P3M  https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/manylinux_2_28/latest

> install.packages('magick')
* installing *binary* package 'magick' ...
* DONE (magick)

> library(magick)
Linking to ImageMagick 6.9.13.25
Enabled features: cairo, fontconfig, freetype, ghostscript, lcms, pango, raw, rsvg, webp, x11

> install.packages('tidyverse')
# all deps install as *binary*
```

P.S. Some R packages with heavy system library dependencies (e.g. `sf`) don't have `manylinux` binaries (only on aarch64?) yet and will fall back to source compilation. But this is a PPM coverage gap, not a rig issue. (E.g., See https://github.com/amazonlinux/amazon-linux-2023/issues/129#issuecomment-3572390465)

title: Support git/github packages
description:
Three possible implementations:
- External git, AFAICT uv does this.
- Use a pure-rust git client like gix (https://crates.io/crates/gix). It seems that gix does not support shallow clones and sparse checkout (FIXME!), which is a problem. gix (with dependencies) is surprisingly large.
- Implement our own git client, essentially port R the code from pkgdepends to rust.

I would rule out gix because it is large and cannot support sparse checkouts and shallow clones. It is not clear that it is worth implementing our own git client, although it would be probably quite simple with Claude. So maybe we can start with an external git.

EDIT: going with external git after all. I might implement a small git client in the future, if installing git is prohibitive.

title: Leave the redhat containers out of the test matrix when the secrets are missing
description:
The `redhat/ubi8`, `redhat/ubi9` and `redhat/ubi10` test jobs register the container with `subscription-manager`, using the `REDHAT_ORG` and `REDHAT_ACTIVATION_KEY_RHEL*` secrets (the `ENVS` block in the Makefile, read by `tests/test-linux-docker.sh`). A pull request from a fork gets no repository secrets, so on every fork PR all six of those jobs stop before running a single test:

```
subscription-manager: error: argument --org: expected one argument
```

That is what happened on #490, #492 and #507.

This leaves the `redhat/*` containers out of the matrix when `REDHAT_ORG` is empty, in both the x86_64 and the aarch64 matrix setup steps, so the jobs are absent rather than red. Pushes, scheduled runs, `workflow_dispatch` and in-repo branches have the secret and keep running them.

Since this PR comes from a fork, its own run shows the effect: the Linux container jobs should list the other fifteen containers and no `redhat/*` ones, and the setup step logs `REDHAT_ORG is not available, leaving out the redhat/* containers`.

title: Skip alias links outside the R root on Windows
description:
Fixes #506.

On Windows in user mode, `find_aliases()` failed the whole command when an `R-release.exe`/`R-oldrel.exe`/`R-next.exe` link pointed at an R outside the current root, because `find_r_version_in_link()` bailed when the target did not start with `get_r_root()` plus a backslash. That took down `rig list`, `rig add`'s already-installed check, and `rig system make-links` whenever `RIG_R_INSTALL_DIR` (or `r-install-dir`) named another root than the one the existing links were made for, and also when it named the same root with forward slashes.

`find_r_version_in_link()` now returns `Option<String>`, with `None` for a file that is not a rig link or whose target is not under the root, and both callers skip such a link, as the macOS and Linux `find_aliases()` already do. `rig system make-links` leaves the link alone rather than deleting it as unused, since it belongs to another root. The version parsing moved into two pure helpers, `user_version_from_link_target()` and `admin_version_from_link_target()`, with unit tests covering the root-prefix match (including case, forward slashes, a different root, and a root that is a prefix of another directory name) and the admin-mode `R-<version>`/`R-devel`/x86_64-on-aarch64 cases.

Checked with `cargo fmt --check`. The two helpers and their tests are plain string code, so I ran them natively on macOS as a standalone `rustc --test` build (both pass); the Windows build itself, and the tests inside `src/windows/mod.rs`, are left to the Windows CI job, which is why this starts as a draft.
